questions.question: What does thermochemistry study?
choices: Reaction speed and the frequency of collisions
The distribution of electrons among atomic orbitals
The separation of mixtures by particle size
Energy changes accompanying chemical processes

questions.question: What is an exothermic process?
choices: A process that releases heat to its surroundings
A process that absorbs heat from its surroundings
A process with no heat exchange
A process with a positive enthalpy change at constant pressure

questions.question: What is an endothermic process?
choices: A process that releases heat to its surroundings
A process with no heat exchange
A process with a negative enthalpy change at constant pressure
A process that absorbs heat from its surroundings

questions.question: What instrument is used to measure heat transfer in a process?
choices: Thermometer alone, without calorimetry measurements
Calorimeter
Barometer
Balance alone, without temperature measurements

questions.question: What does specific heat capacity describe?
choices: The energy required to melt a unit mass at fixed temperature
The rate of heat transfer through a surface
Energy needed to raise one unit of mass by one degree
The total heat a material contains at every temperature

questions.question: At constant pressure, what sign of enthalpy change indicates an exothermic reaction?
choices: Positive
Always zero
Undefined for every reaction
Negative

questions.question: In a thermochemistry experiment, what is the system?
choices: Only the room outside the selected materials
Only the thermometer, regardless of the process
The material or process selected for study
All surroundings except the reacting materials

questions.question: Why does breaking a chemical bond require energy?
choices: Energy is needed to overcome attractions holding bonded atoms together
Breaking bonds always releases stored energy
Bond breaking occurs only without energy transfer
Bond energy depends only on the reactants' total mass

questions.question: What generally happens when new chemical bonds form?
choices: Energy must always be absorbed
Energy is released
No energy changes accompany bond formation
The release always equals the energy used to break reactant bonds

questions.question: Why can a reaction release heat even though bond breaking requires energy?
choices: Exothermic reactions do not require any bond breaking
Breaking bonds releases more energy than forming bonds
Bond formation releases more energy than bond breaking absorbs
All reactant bonds have exactly the same energy as product bonds

questions.question: How are system and surroundings energy changes related in an isolated overall setup?
choices: Both must gain the same amount of energy
Energy lost by one is gained by the other
Both must lose the same amount of energy
The system's heat loss is unrelated to the surroundings

questions.question: What does a warming surrounding solution suggest about a reaction, if other heat sources are absent?
choices: The reaction absorbs heat from that solution
The reaction has no energy change
The reaction necessarily forms a gas
The reaction releases heat

questions.question: Why must calorimetry calculations consider heat escaping to the room?
choices: It can cause measured heat transfer to underestimate the reaction's heat release
It guarantees a larger measured temperature rise
It changes the reaction's balanced equation
It increases the heat remaining in the calorimeter

questions.question: What distinguishes activation energy from enthalpy change?
choices: Activation energy is a barrier; enthalpy change compares initial and final states
Both always equal the final temperature
Enthalpy change measures only collision frequency
Activation energy determines only product mass

questions.question: Why do melting and freezing have opposite heat-transfer directions?
choices: Both processes always release energy
Both processes always absorb energy
Melting absorbs energy and freezing releases energy
Neither process involves particle arrangements

questions.question: A 100 g sample with specific heat 4 J/(g·°C) warms by 5°C. How much energy does it absorb?
A system releases 80 J to its surroundings. What is the system's energy change from that transfer?
choices: 0 J

questions.question: A reaction's products have lower enthalpy than its reactants. Which conclusion follows?
choices: The reaction is endothermic
The reaction is exothermic
Its activation energy must be zero
Its atoms have disappeared

questions.question: Equal masses of two substances receive equal heat with no heat loss. Which warms less?
choices: The one with higher specific heat capacity
The one with lower specific heat capacity
Both must warm equally
The one with the lower starting volume in every case

questions.question: Reaction A releases 40 kJ per mole and reaction B absorbs 40 kJ per mole. For one mole of each, what is the net heat exchange?
choices: 80 kJ released
80 kJ absorbed
0 kJ
40 kJ released
